Definition: from G2637; to be a traducer, i.e. to slander:--speak against (evil of).
BiblicalUsage: To speak against is to slander a brother, and James says whoever speaks evil of his brother speaks evil of the law and judges the law. Peter turns it around: keep your conversation honest among the Gentiles, so that where they speak against you as evildoers, they may glorify God when they see your good works, and those who falsely accuse your good conversation in Christ may be ashamed. The tongue is judged by the life behind it.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe speaking against my brother is really speaking against the law that commands me to love him. I hold that the best answer to slander is a life that shames it, because good works outlast evil words.
